sidePlacement.method: Each named side (NS, SS, ES, WS, NS/WS, SES, …) goes on the side of the line whose outward normal is closest to that compass direction, length weighted. When the direction runs within ~20° of the street (conf < 0.35), the City's word is ambiguous: the side is the one the block's street sweeping tickets of the past year carry (house number parity, on dates only that rule sweeps; 5 tickets and 80% to decide), else the same street's with the same schedule text, else the compass guess stays. "Every Tues & Wed" names no side: split by the tickets the same way (each day on the side its tickets are on), else both sides both days.

crossCheck.note: Street sweeping tickets (86.0112(E)) of the last 12 months in the City's citation data, which has the date and the typed address but no time. Each ticket goes on the posted block of its street whose numbers hold it, on the side holding its parity; "sideSweptThatDay" = that side has a rule on that date (weekday, week of the month, month). Tickets are written only where a sign says no parking that day, so this is how we know the schedule is the one on the signs.

sideSwapCandidates.note: Blocks where the City names both sides clearly but the tickets on both sides are on the other side (5 tickets and 80% each, on dates only that rule sweeps): the sides look swapped in the schedule, or the signs differ from it. Swapped to follow the tickets (--as-published keeps the City's text); a question for the City.
